Guillermo's own take for Tue, Oct 27 (his read, quote it as his, not yours): Only one forecast calls for a southerly day in Squamish (it happens to be the one that works better on this area, but none of the others aligned). Environment Canada has Howe Sound southerly 10 to 20 near noon, and the outflow is gone: Pam Rocks reads N 2 at 7am and Pemberton is a touch below Vancouver.

My best guess today is the Nexen from noon to about 4pm, SSW 13 to 14 gusting 17. Low tide is 11ft at 1pm. It’s grey all day, so don’t expect extra thermal. If the Spit vane is south and reading 10+ by 11am, drive up.

English Bay buoy reads W 10 gusting 12, ahead of the page’s 6. If it hits 12+ by 10am, Jericho could be a foil option.

EC marine forecast, Howe Sound (issued 04:00 AM PDT 27 October 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Today Tonight and Wednesday. Strong wind warning in effect. Wind light increasing to southerly inflow 10 to 20 knots near noon then becoming northerly outflow 10 to 15 near midnight. Wind increasing to northerly outflow 15 to 25 Wednesday evening.

EC marine forecast, Strait of Georgia (south of Nanaimo) (issued 04:00 AM PDT 27 October 2026): Today Tonight and Wednesday. Wind northwest 10 to 15 knots becoming southwest 10 to 20 this afternoon then becoming northwest 5 to 15 near midnight. Wind becoming light Wednesday morning then becoming southeast 5 to 15 Wednesday afternoon.
